measured_by: streaming/ applications on the 3-VM Kafka cluster (scripts/gcp_stream.ps1)

cluster.mode: KRaft (each node is broker and controller)
cluster.consumers: group of 3 scorers, offsets committed after the alerts are delivered (at-least-once)

known.description: model trained on 80 % of the sample, replay of the 20 % held out (all attack families are known to the model)

unseen.description: model trained on the days before 2018-02-28, replay of 2018-02-28 and later (Infilteration and Bot never seen)

fault_tolerance_test.action: sfumato-kafka-3 (one broker and one scorer) stopped at 11:15:14 while 300 flows/s were flowing, restarted at 11:18:25
fault_tolerance_test.during_failure: the two remaining scorers took over the 6 partitions (0-1-2 and 3-4-5) and kept consuming
fault_tolerance_test.after_restart: the restarted VM rejoined the group (partitions 4-5) and the consumer lag of the three scorers fell to about 15-20 messages each
limits: Only one broker failure was tested (replication 3, min in-sync 2 tolerates one).
The counters of the restarted scorer restart from zero, so cumulative totals are not comparable across the restart.
Processing is at-least-once: a few flows may be scored twice after a failover.
No data-loss audit (sent versus processed exactly) was performed.

throughput.note: 300 flows/s was the tested rate, not a measured maximum

stress_tests.conditions: 3 Kafka VMs running brokers, scorers and the regular 300 flows/s replay producer; Flink not yet running
stress_tests.limit_seen: producer on one VM (6,463 of 7,200 flows/s produced); the scorers kept up
method_flaws: the regular producer's 300 flows/s was counted inside the target
backlog left from the previous activity distorted the first step
only one scorer state was fresh at the start

stress_tests.conditions: same 3 VMs, plus Flink reading the same topic and application logs shipped to Logstash; 3 scorers active, background producer subtracted, backlog purged before the first step
stress_tests.limit_seen: producer on one VM (lower bound: the scorers kept up)
stress_tests.reading: The two runs differ (6,463 versus 4,078 flows/s) because the load on the three small VMs differs (Flink and log shipping were added) and because the producer, not the scorers, is the limit: treat the figures as lower bounds of this setup, not as a capacity guarantee.

jobs: rule-alerts (bursts of >= 200 flows shorter than 1 s per port in 10 s, DNS excluded)
flink.caveat: labelled replay with 62 % attacks; on real traffic these port-burst rules would produce many false positives without source addresses and history

qwen.note: rules answer shown first, model rewrite replaces it when it arrives
